subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should Birdclaw own third-party passive-capture import, and if so should the supported MVP be limited to Scrollmark canonical bundle v1?
rationale: The local-data direction aligns with VISION.md, but permanent support obligations, provenance schema, account association, and whether unversioned legacy exports belong in core require maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor bundle v1 first
options.body: Support only Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially and treat legacy Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter formats as later, separately justified compatibility work.

options.title: Sponsor all proposed formats
options.body: Accept canonical and legacy formats in one feature, with a larger parser, fixture, migration, and compatibility commitment.

options.title: Keep official sources only
options.body: Limit core imports to official archives, Birdclaw backups, and existing live transports, leaving third-party conversion to external tooling.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bundle v1 first
recommendation.body: Support only Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially and treat legacy Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter formats as later, separately justified compatibility work.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the documented product vision and the current archive/canonical-store direction.
